To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the proteome of resistant P. strobus seedlings is enriched in proteins with known roles or homologs of known roles in disease-resistance, and that the most abundant protein in resistant seedlings is a homolog of a protein with a leucine-rich domain.

we have discovered that the LRR superfamily of proteins, which are known to have roles in disease resistance in many plant species, are upregulated in blister rust resistant white pine and are likely to play a role in resistance to white pine blister rust in Pinus strobas.

the first proteomic analysis of white pine blister rust resistant Pinus strobus needles revealed 13 proteins with a > or = 3 fold increase in resistant needles in comparison to needles of susceptible seedlings.

the results of this study provide evidence that a hypersensitive-like response is involved in resistance to white pine blister rust in Pinus strobas.

we have identified several candidate proteins for further investigation as potential disease resistance genes in white pine blister rust.
